above_gcse.text: This matters. Temperature measures the average KE per particle. Internal energy (the thermal store) depends on temperature AND the number of particles AND the spacing between them.
above_gcse.why: The specification sections given (4.1.1.3, 4.3.2.1, 4.3.2.2) do not link temperature to average particle kinetic energy. They also do not say internal energy depends on particle spacing. The spec defines internal energy only as 'the total kinetic energy and potential energy of all the particles (atoms and molecules) that make up a system'. The extra dependence on spacing is not explained, and it could confuse the student.

above_gcse.text: Temperature is a measure of the average kinetic energy of the particles.
above_gcse.why: This is not required by the sections given. It also clashes with the lesson's own keyTerms definition: 'It is related to the average kinetic energy of the particles'. Strictly, temperature is related to the average kinetic energy of the particles' random motion; it is not a direct measure of it. That nuance goes beyond these sections, so the two different wordings may confuse the student.
